Before you mesh, look at what SCGSim read from your plan: one table for the
conductors and regions, with each one's Net, material and height, then the Net
membership, the material properties and the port sheets. A Net you forgot, a
wrong material or a vacuum region of the wrong size shows here, before any
solver runs, and nothing is built.

## Show the summary {#summary}

Pass the snapshot of a prepared plan, here the square pad of
[Prepare a layout](prepare-a-layout.qmd#example):

```python
from IPython.display import display
from scgsim.geometry import summarize_geometry_input

summary = summarize_geometry_input(
    snapshot.geometry_input, prepared_stack=snapshot.stack
)
display(summary)
```

In a notebook it shows these tables. For the square pad, the first one reads:

| Entity | Occurrence | Net | Material | Kind | Z range (µm) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D0_SUBSTRATE | unknown | unknown | Si | dielectric | -500–0 | solution_region |
| VACUUM_REGION | unknown | unknown | vacuum | vacuum | -1500–1000.1 | solution_region |
| chip/PAD | chip | pad | Al | conductor | 0–0.1 | metal |
| chip/GROUND | chip | ground | Al | conductor | 0–0.1 | metal |

So the pad and the ground are 0.1 µm of aluminium on a 500 µm silicon
substrate, in the Nets `pad` and `ground`, and the vacuum region reaches 1000 µm
below the substrate and 1000 µm above the metal, as the padding
`(0.0, 0.0, 1000.0)` asked. The substrate and the vacuum belong to no Net,
which the table shows as `unknown`: a value that was not set is shown as
unknown, never as zero.

The next tables list the Net membership (`ground`: `chip/GROUND`; `pad`:
`chip/PAD`), the properties of each material (silicon with permittivity 11.9,
aluminium with its conductivity) and the port sheets. The square pad has one,
`chip/o_junction_lumped`, lying on `chip/PAD` and `chip/GROUND` on layer
`D0_TOP_M1`.

This summary shows the source only. Its junction and Surface-EPR tables stay
empty whatever the plan sets with `set_rectangular_junctions` or
`set_surface_epr`, and it has no solver settings: an empty table here does not
mean the setting is missing. To check those settings, use `sim.input_summary()`
(below).

`summary.data` holds the same content as a dictionary for a script. It is a
copy: editing it changes nothing in the snapshot.

## With the simulation's settings {#with-settings}

Once a simulation is set up, `sim.input_summary()` shows the same tables with
its own settings added. A Palace simulation shows the input as `mesh()` will
build it: with its route and approximation profile, the plan's Surface-EPR
request, and only the ports the simulation uses. `EigenmodeSim` lists each port
with its inductance, and `ElectrostaticSim` its terminals, grounds and
policies; an AEDT `EigenmodeSim` lists the plan's Surface-EPR request and its
junctions. After `write_config()`, the run's index map says which conductor
became which terminal; see
[Palace: terminal capacitance](capacitance-palace.qmd).

## Keep the source with your results {#retain-a-portable-paired-source}

A snapshot carries the GDS file and the layer stack it was built from. Saving
both lets a later session read the same source without the PDK or GDSFactory.
Give each study you keep its own new folder: `exist_ok=False` refuses a folder
that already exists, so a later study never replaces the files of an earlier
one.

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.geometry import build_gds_stack_geometry_input

source_dir = Path(".artifacts/sources/square-pad-20um")  # a new folder per study
source_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
gds_path = source_dir / "model.gds"
stack_path = source_dir / "model.stack.json"
gds_path.write_bytes(snapshot.gds_bytes)
stack_path.write_text(json.dumps(snapshot.stack, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
reloaded = build_gds_stack_geometry_input(
    gds_file=gds_path,
    stack_file=stack_path,
    top_cell_name=snapshot.stack["metadata"]["top_cell_name"],
)
print(tuple(entity.semantic_id for entity in reloaded.entities))
```

Keep the two files together: the stack holds the polygons read from that GDS,
so reading it with another GDS is refused, with both files' SHA-256 digests in
the message.

Next, [check the layout](check-a-layout.qmd), or after `mesh()`
[inspect the prepared model](inspect-the-prepared-model.qmd).
